title: VCRI Facilities Asset Assessment Methodology v1

grades.meaning: Best-in-class facilities posture. Inventoried, access-controlled, monitored, resilient, and attested physical and OT estate across all dimensions. No critical findings.
Solid facilities posture. Documented controls across most dimensions; minor gaps in 1-2 areas with remediation paths defined. Suitable for production reliance with stated caveats.
Acceptable with conditions. Notable gaps in 2-3 dimensions; remediation roadmap required. Not suitable for high-assurance physical/OT reliance without compensating controls.
Significant gaps across multiple dimensions. Physical/OT risk is material; remediation required before high-assurance reliance.
Material failure of facilities posture. Physical and cyber-physical exposure is unmanaged; reliance not recommended in current state.

subcriteria.title: Facility and building-system inventory
anchors: No facility inventory; building systems (BMS, HVAC, access control, OT/IoT) are undocumented.
Partial inventory kept ad-hoc for some sites; building systems largely uncatalogued.
An inventory standard is defined but inconsistently maintained; OT/IoT coverage drifts from reality.
Documented inventory of in-scope sites and building/OT systems (vendor, model, firmware) consistently maintained.
All of #3 plus automated discovery of networked building/OT assets and periodic reconciliation audits.
All of #4 plus continuous asset discovery with independently validated inventory completeness.

subcriteria.title: Building/OT system provenance and SBOM
anchors: No provenance for building/OT systems; origin and software composition unknown.
Provenance noted ad-hoc for a few systems; no SBOM collection.
A provenance/SBOM standard for building-OT vendors is defined but inconsistently collected.
Vendor/firmware provenance and SBOMs consistently collected for in-scope building/OT systems.
All of #3 plus SBOMs validated and tracked for known vulnerabilities, with audited coverage.
All of #4 plus cryptographically attested firmware provenance independently verifiable.

subcriteria.title: Third-party facility and OT vendor governance
anchors: Facility and building-system vendors operate ungoverned; remote-access and maintenance uncontrolled.
Some vendor arrangements exist informally; no consistent security requirements.
Facility/OT vendor security requirements are defined but inconsistently enforced.
Documented security requirements and access governance consistently applied to facility/OT vendors.
All of #3 plus technical control of vendor remote access and periodic audit of vendor compliance.
All of #4 plus independent attestation of facility/OT vendor controls and continuous monitoring of vendor access.

subcriteria.title: Physical access control and badging
anchors: Doors are unlocked or use shared keys; no badge system; entry is unattributable.
Badge or key control applied ad-hoc at some sites; sharing and untracked keys common.
A physical-access standard (individual badges, access logs) is defined but inconsistently applied across sites.
Individual badge-based access with logging documented and consistently enforced across in-scope sites.
All of #3 plus centralized badge lifecycle management, zone-based least access, and audited access logs.
All of #4 plus continuously governed physical access with independently attested controls.

subcriteria.title: Multi-factor physical access to sensitive areas
anchors: Sensitive areas (server rooms, OT spaces) have no stronger control than general areas.
Extra controls applied ad-hoc to a few sensitive areas; inconsistent.
A multi-factor physical-access standard for sensitive areas is defined but inconsistently enforced.
Multi-factor physical access (badge + PIN/biometric) documented and consistently enforced for in-scope sensitive areas.
All of #3 plus anti-tailgating measures, access-pattern review, and audited enforcement.
All of #4 plus continuously verified, behavior-aware physical access with independent attestation.

subcriteria.title: Building-system credential and identity management
anchors: Building/OT systems use default or shared credentials; logins are unattributable.
Some default credentials changed ad-hoc; many systems remain on shared/default logins.
A building-system credential standard is defined but inconsistently applied across OT/BMS.
Unique, managed credentials and individual identity for in-scope building/OT systems consistently enforced.
All of #3 plus centralized OT identity/secret management, rotation, and audited usage.
All of #4 plus hardware-backed building-system identity independently attested.

subcriteria.title: Physical privacy controls
anchors: No physical privacy controls; sensitive discussions and materials are exposed in open areas.
Clean-desk and meeting-room practices applied ad-hoc at some sites.
A physical-privacy standard (clean desk, secure rooms for sensitive work) is defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented physical-privacy controls consistently applied across in-scope sites (secure rooms, screening, soundproofing where warranted).
All of #3 plus audited compliance (e.g., clean-desk checks) and physical-privacy zones defined and enforced.
All of #4 plus privacy-by-design facility architecture with independently validated controls.

subcriteria.title: Surveillance and visitor data minimization
anchors: Surveillance (CCTV) and visitor records are collected and retained without limit or policy.
Some retention practice exists ad-hoc; minimization not considered.
A minimization/retention standard for surveillance and visitor data is defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented minimization and retention for surveillance/visitor data consistently applied across in-scope sites.
All of #3 plus enforced retention limits, access controls on footage, and audited compliance.
All of #4 plus minimized-by-design surveillance with independently validated retention/access governance.

subcriteria.title: Privacy-by-design in facility architecture
anchors: Facility design ignores privacy; layouts expose sensitive work and people.
Privacy considered ad-hoc in some renovations; no standard.
Privacy-by-design facility requirements are defined but inconsistently applied to new build/renovation.
Privacy-by-design consistently applied to in-scope facility changes (segregated visitor areas, sightline control).
All of #3 plus design reviews for surveillance minimization and audited adherence.
All of #4 plus continuously improved privacy-by-design standards independently validated.

subcriteria.title: Physical perimeter and intrusion protection
anchors: No physical perimeter protection; intrusion is trivial and undetected.
Basic locks and barriers applied ad-hoc; no consistent perimeter standard.
A perimeter-protection standard (barriers, locks, intrusion detection) is defined but inconsistently implemented.
Documented perimeter protection with intrusion detection consistently implemented across in-scope sites.
All of #3 plus monitored intrusion alarms with response procedures and audited perimeter integrity.
All of #4 plus layered, continuously monitored perimeter defense independently validated.

subcriteria.title: OT/building-system network segmentation
anchors: Building/OT systems sit on flat networks reachable from IT or the internet; no segmentation.
Some segmentation applied ad-hoc; OT/IT separation is incomplete and porous.
An OT-segmentation standard is defined but inconsistently enforced; gaps and undocumented connections persist.
Documented OT/IT segmentation consistently enforced for in-scope building/OT systems.
All of #3 plus monitored segmentation boundaries, controlled OT remote access, and audited segmentation integrity.
All of #4 plus zero-trust OT architecture with continuous verification independently attested.

subcriteria.title: Environmental protection (power, HVAC, fire)
anchors: Critical spaces lack environmental protection; power, cooling, and fire risks are unmanaged.
Some environmental controls exist ad-hoc; no standard or testing.
An environmental-protection standard (UPS, HVAC, fire suppression) is defined but inconsistently implemented.
Documented environmental controls for critical in-scope spaces consistently implemented.
All of #3 plus monitored environmental systems with alerting and audited protection coverage.
All of #4 plus resilient, continuously monitored environmental protection independently validated.

subcriteria.title: Life-safety and physical safety systems
anchors: No managed life-safety systems (fire detection, emergency egress, alarms); occupant safety is unaddressed.
Life-safety equipment present but maintained ad-hoc; testing irregular.
A life-safety standard is defined but inconsistently maintained and tested.
Documented life-safety systems consistently maintained and tested for in-scope sites.
All of #3 plus monitored life-safety systems, regular drills, and audited maintenance/testing records.
All of #4 plus continuously monitored, independently inspected and attested life-safety assurance.

subcriteria.title: Facility resilience and redundancy
anchors: No redundancy; loss of power or cooling halts operations with no fallback.
Some redundancy exists ad-hoc; untested and incomplete.
A resilience standard (backup power, cooling redundancy) is defined but inconsistently implemented or tested.
Documented redundancy for critical in-scope facilities consistently implemented (backup power, cooling).
All of #3 plus tested failover (generator/UPS/cooling tests), measured recovery, and audited resilience.
All of #4 plus geographically/architecturally resilient facilities with independently validated continuity.

subcriteria.title: OT/building-system integrity and failsafe
anchors: Building/OT systems can fail or be manipulated into unsafe states with no failsafe.
Failsafe behavior addressed ad-hoc on a few systems; no standard.
An OT-integrity/failsafe standard is defined but inconsistently implemented.
Documented OT integrity and failsafe behavior consistently implemented for in-scope critical systems.
All of #3 plus monitored OT integrity with anomaly alerting and audited failsafe validation.
All of #4 plus continuously verified OT integrity with independently attested failsafe assurance.

subcriteria.title: Physical surveillance and monitoring
anchors: No physical surveillance or monitoring; physical incidents go undetected.
Some CCTV/monitoring exists ad-hoc; footage unreviewed and uncoordinated.
A physical-monitoring standard is defined but inconsistently applied; coverage has gaps.
Documented physical surveillance and monitoring consistently deployed across in-scope sites with retention.
All of #3 plus monitored alerts, integration with response, and audited coverage.
All of #4 plus analytics-driven physical monitoring (anomaly detection) with independently validated coverage.

subcriteria.title: OT/building-system threat detection and response
anchors: No detection or response capability for threats to building/OT systems.
OT incidents handled improvised; no monitoring or plan.
An OT detection/response standard is defined but untested and inconsistently applied.
Documented OT threat detection and response consistently maintained for in-scope building/OT systems.
All of #3 plus OT-specific monitoring (e.g., OT-aware IDS), tested response, and audited readiness.
All of #4 plus continuous OT threat monitoring with measured detection/response and independently validated readiness.

subcriteria.title: Facility/OT vulnerability and patch management
anchors: Building/OT systems are never patched or checked; exposure is unknown and accumulating.
Patching/hardening of OT happens ad-hoc and reactively; no standard.
An OT patch/secure-configuration standard is defined but inconsistently applied; drift common.
Documented patch and secure-baseline management consistently applied to in-scope building/OT systems.
All of #3 plus scheduled OT vulnerability assessment, tracked remediation (with compensating controls where patching is constrained), and audit.
All of #4 plus continuous OT posture management with independently attested configuration.
